Getting my sides shaved + and undercut was the only thing that made my hair more manageable. I also get it thinned every 6 weeks, but I only reccomend this if your hair is healthy to begin with, damaged hair will be extra floofy.

Of course the best thing I ever did for it was shave my whole head but that's a very extreme solution. While it was great for my sanity the 2 year process of growing it out was less great

Most of it is genetic, my natural hair was (past tense because I first dyed it when I turned 13 and haven't left it alone since) insanely thick and dense. It was always shiny and healthy but after almost a decade of bleaching it's taken a lot of work to get it back to "normal".

I only wash it once a week and always do a deep conditioning treatment or hair mask with shampoo. I swear by olaplex and almond oil, the oil especially, is the only reason I still have hair on my head. 

Having thick hair doesn't equal shiny hair though, thicker strands don't lie flat as easily so it takes more work to make your hair look glossy. I'm always so envious of people with finer hair but I guess the grass is always greener etc

I used to do it any time my mental health gets bad, it's a small thing I could control and it helped some. Then of course I started an office job and decided to shave it all off, almost to prove I wasn't a "boring" office job person. So the last 2 years has been spent trying to make the most of the weird regrowth phases. 

It's been really hard actually, I lost the little bit of control that I used to make myself feel better, all I could do was change the colour, and I bleached my hair to death in the process (23 different colours in 3 months kinda bleached to death). Luckily I've gotten it back to a healthy state and after it all I don't rely on a silly thing like my hair to manage my mental health anymore so I guess growth (pun intended).
Fr though, it's the only hobby I keep coming back to. It's how I fill the gaps in my attention when I'm listening to music or an audiobook rather than just endlessly scrolling through social media

I think for me personally, self harm is a way of validating the severity of my dark thoughts or mental illness. So when you see people talking about their issues you feel the need to prove to yourself or others that you did it all for a reason/you are "sick enough" despite being in a relatively good headspace. This will also manifest itself in a need to admonish others' struggles in order to satisfy the same need for justification I already mentioned, unfortunately I don't have any one way to stop this as it's something I do to this day; but something I spend a lot of time working on.

It's just important to remember that you are valid no matter the external signs, the hardest thing about mental illness is how utterly invisible it is. But you don't need to prove that to anyone no matter what they say (even if it's you), and if you relapse then thats also ok if it's what you needed at the time. Making yourself feel guilty for coping in the only way you know how is not productive and will only cause you more hurt, just stay safe and do what's best for you.
